note: Reviewed cutoff windows. A window is a precise journal phase, not a community: the affected quest's own phase graph has a connected Failure input, and that input is gated by the closer's journal. tools/review_cutoffs.py validates every window against tools/quest_index.json and the graph; the app reads the result from data/cutoffs.json. Nothing here is wiki-derived.

windows.action: Give both statuettes to Triss during Final Preparations
windows.headline: Hand both statuettes to Triss before Final Preparations ends
windows.why: When Battle Preparations begins, the game's own fixup graph runs a branch for each statuette journal entry: the branch reads q210preparations.journal as Active or Success and sends the entry through a Success or Failure input. That is the game resolving the quests, not an NPC silently disappearing. Triss takes the statuettes during Final Preparations after the Philippa rescue (the statuette phase tests q310_philippa_rescued), so that quest is the last window.
files: quests\bugfixing_phase.w2phase: journal blocks 6832 (noble) and 6796 (soldier) have connected Failure inputs fed by conditions 6828/6800; their shared pause condition 6808 ('q210 preparation complete') tests q210preparations.journal as Active or Success
gameplay\journal\quests\q210preparations.journal is Battle Preparations; its first phase is Novigrad ('Meet Avallac'h on the ship')

quests\minor_quests\novigrad\mq3012_jade_statuettes.w2phase is the turn-in; it tests q310_philippa_rescued and q310_keira_done, and its own phase activates triss.w2comm, so Now or Never's switch is a phase transition, not a cutoff
caveats: No save in the corpus has a statuette still open when Battle Preparations starts, so the save history cannot confirm the window; the game's own connected Failure branch is the evidence.
Before the window the journal can say Active for a long time: the quest is still winnable, not lost.
After the window, if the journal still says Active, the app says CHECK NOW rather than LOST; only a Failed journal entry may be called lost.
